sections: A fresh map, from the world data
The region grid and essential connections
From the master to detailed crops

sites.name: The Winding Lowlands
sites.visual: A broad low-lying landscape of winding channels, lake edges, scattered homesteads and one very small inhabited settlement. Include a modest green, winding lane, landing and simple crossing as parts of the same lowland scene.
sites.note: This pin represents a landscape and its tiny settlement, not one oversized building. Preserve a water-linked approach and generous open ground.

sites.name: Greywatch Keep
sites.visual: A broken gate and weathered defensive walls surround an overgrown yard, with roofless stone rooms and a damaged upper rampart. It is an obsolete founding-era fort above the western approaches.
sites.note: A compact historic ruin, smaller than an academy campus. No functioning garrison, new military town or invented giant dungeon.

sites.name: Moonwhisker Emporium
sites.visual: A modest city pet-and-companion shop with a practical storefront. Suggest its identity through small carriers, a sheltered entry or an enclosed service yard; the actual perches and feed bins are inside.
sites.note: One shop footprint among surrounding roofs. Do not render giant cages, loose legendary animals or a whole zoo.

sites.name: Stargarden Manor
sites.visual: The Great Sage's private residence, approached through a quiet front garden. A composed house, reception side, private residential wing and secluded rear garden distinguish domestic life from civic government.
sites.note: A separate residence from the Grand Sage's Court and Sage's Spire. Its near-boundary pin places it close to the civic district, not in a remote estate province.

sites.name: The Emberfox Hot Spring
sites.visual: A modest bathing house beside warm outdoor pools on the western outskirts. Let rock, vegetation and a faint trace of steam establish the retreat; ordinary timber construction suits its rural setting.
sites.note: The bathing house must remain comparable to other small buildings. Do not turn the pools into an enormous palace or volcanic crater.

sites.name: Phoenix Wing Academy
sites.visual: A compact academy precinct marked by red pennants, connected teaching wings, a broad arrival court and open practice grounds. Distinguish the training yard and small practice arena from the city's great public colosseum.
sites.note: Dining, dormitories, faculty offices, commons and music room belong to this one campus. Use a few coordinated roofs around courts rather than eleven independent landmarks.

sites.name: Evertree Base
sites.visual: One immense living tree rises directly from the ground beside and behind the court precinct. Show a rooted trunk, a coherent canopy and palace-adjacent approaches; the rootward courtyard belongs beneath it.
sites.note: The tree is the single dominant magical landmark, with a limited canopy that does not swallow the city. The vaulted Portal Room is below the rootward structures, not a second outdoor portal monument.

sites.name: Sage's Spire
sites.visual: The Great Sage's working tower and office beside the court and Evertree grounds. Give it a clear vertical silhouette and a plausible stair-and-office volume, separated from the living tree.
sites.note: This is an office tower, not the Evertree itself and not the Great Sage's private manor. Let it support the main skyline rather than compete with it.

sites.name: The Grand Sage's Court
sites.visual: A civic palace precinct with a formal forecourt facing the ascending avenue, public galleries and office wings. Evertree grounds lie behind it. A compact observatory can rise above the offices, subordinate to the tree.
sites.note: Government, council and audience rooms are inside this complex. Keep the court, nearby tower office and tree base distinct but physically coherent.

sites.name: Briarcrest Manor
sites.visual: A substantial residential manor with an entrance walk, formal reception side and garden grounds. Its clear garden boundary separates it from the adjoining upper-city roofs.
sites.note: One residence and its grounds; its for-sale status does not need signage on the map. Keep its scale below the civic palace.

sites.name: The Gilded Griffin
sites.visual: A fine jewelry shop with a polished, restrained frontage and a formal entrance. Its display salon and fitting desk occupy the interior.
sites.note: A small high-quality commercial building, not a gilded castle or giant griffin statue.

sites.name: Cloud District
sites.visual: An upper civic residential neighborhood of fine homes, polished streets, garden squares and terraced lanes around the court. The defining quality is an ensemble of orderly residences, not a cloud platform.
sites.note: Spread ordinary houses across a district-sized patch. It is neither a separate city nor a floating island.

sites.name: The Magistrate's Hall
sites.visual: A substantial but practical civic hall with tall windows, a public vestibule and a clear public approach. Records and hearing rooms sit behind the frontage.
sites.note: One civic building with several internal rooms; use an orderly street-facing silhouette rather than a fortress or prison.

sites.name: Rune and Raven's
sites.visual: A magical-accessory and focus shop with a tidy public frontage and a working bench deeper inside. Glass display bays and a discreet workshop addition provide its commercial identity.
sites.note: One compact shop. Do not scale its sample focuses into giant rooftop artifacts.

sites.name: House Goldbarrow Estate
sites.visual: A noble residence set behind a gate and formal front gardens, with private grounds and a residence hall. Its enclosed garden footprint gives it more breathing room than ordinary city housing.
sites.note: A household estate, not a second governing palace. The name does not require gold-covered buildings.

sites.name: The Grand Ascent
sites.visual: A monumental stair avenue climbs from the bazaar toward the palace forecourt. Broad intermediate landings provide views and a convincing change in elevation.
sites.note: An exposed circulation feature, not another palace. Its pin lies on the court-bazaar axis; its full route spans beyond the point marker.

sites.name: The Arcane Emporium
sites.visual: The city's largest and fanciest magic shop. A grand entrance and broader gallery volume distinguish it from the smaller commercial premises nearby.
sites.note: A large shop within the urban grain. Curated rooms and consultation salons do not become separate freestanding towers.

sites.name: Bramble & Bottle
sites.visual: A potion shop fitted into a city block. A small glazed storefront or sheltered display entrance can suggest a bottle gallery, with the preparation workroom behind.
sites.note: One compact premises. Optional bottle-colored accents are a visual interpretation, not a required roof color or new landmark.

sites.name: The Wandering Quill
sites.visual: A small stationery shop within the civic-commercial streets. A narrow frontage, neat entrance and attached roof can imply paper and ink trade without readable text.
sites.note: Draw as one ordinary shop, with stock and counter inside. Its neighboring streets matter more than a giant quill emblem.

sites.name: Clovermead
sites.visual: A small northern farming settlement with a few houses scattered among broad cultivated fields. A waterside landing and intervening water explain why people reach it by boat.
sites.note: Do not connect it to the city with a new ordinary road bridge. Keep its houses as small as comparable city homes.

sites.name: Pinewake Coast
sites.visual: A northern coastal strip where pines reach the shore. Include a dry upper path, small headland, tide pools and uneven exposed rock shelves.
sites.note: Let the terrain carry this location. It does not need a new village, lighthouse or castle.

sites.name: Beaconrest Lighthouse
sites.visual: A red-capped working lighthouse stands on a small offshore rock with a low supply jetty and attached keeper's quarters. Its signal balcony and lantern room give it a readable profile.
sites.note: It is a slender navigation marker, not a tower the size of the city arena. Keep it detached from the mainland by a water channel.

sites.name: Rosetimber Suburbs
sites.visual: A pleasant, prosperous residential neighborhood adjoining the Cloud District. Set individual homes among maintained gardens and controlled lanes, below the grandeur of the noble estates.
sites.note: An inhabited neighborhood, not one manor or another walled town. Its boundary with nearby residential districts may be gradual.

sites.name: Whitecrest Harbor
sites.visual: A working waterfront of cargo steps, quays, sheds, loading space and passenger access, with moored craft scaled to the buildings. Shore roads and city lanes meet the quay network.
sites.note: Draw an operational harbor district rather than one giant building or a forest of oversized masts. Keep navigable channels open toward the islands.

sites.name: Hydra Head Academy
sites.visual: A garden-oriented academy precinct with violet awnings, a welcoming court and connected halls arranged around group-work spaces. Landscaped walks and a pavilion make its exterior distinct.
sites.note: Keep the indoor practice hall, lecture rooms, dormitories and dining facilities within the campus. It is not an enormous botanical country estate.

sites.name: Wraith Island
sites.visual: A small, isolated skull-shaped rocky island receives controlled supply boats at Skullshore Landing. A compact prison approach can be visible, subordinate to the rock's outline.
sites.note: Keep the island small and distinct from the inhabited islands. The separate playable prison realm is not another island to duplicate on this map.

sites.name: Driftstone Isle
sites.visual: A rocky offshore island with a small resident community, modest homes and a water-facing landing. Ordinary island life is the defining feature.
sites.note: A separate inhabited island from Saltmere; avoid a second prison, giant ruin or duplicate skull rock.

sites.name: Saltmere
sites.visual: A small inhabited island village: compact houses cluster near a working shore and landing, with enough rocky ground to read as its own island.
sites.note: Separate it from Driftstone Isle and Wraith Island. It must not disappear into the harbor mainland.

sites.name: Bluecoil Rest
sites.visual: A remote reef with inner ledges, clear surrounding water, a narrow wash shore and an outlying mooring rock. The inner rocks form the fixed resting habitat of the great blue serpent Nerathyl.
sites.note: The reef is the durable landmark. If the serpent is shown, keep it a secondary sleeping coil at believable map scale; do not create a giant monster island or imply multiple serpents.

sites.name: The Gilded Albatross
sites.visual: An ornate but hard-used sailing ship at a charted anchorage, with a main working deck, raised quarterdeck and visible rigging. Salvage equipment and practical crew circulation matter more than pristine decoration.
sites.note: A ship, never an island or town. Its galley, hold and cabins are below or within the same hull. Crew and captain are not giant portrait figures on the map.

sites.name: West City Gate
sites.visual: A guarded western arch connects city paving to the wilderness and caravan road. Its masonry and adjoining wall establish the city's western threshold.
sites.note: Attach it to the main city wall. It is not an independent castle or another town.

sites.name: Wayfarer's Goods
sites.visual: A practical travel-supply shop among western city streets, with a modest loading edge and a functional frontage for road equipment.
sites.note: One city shop. Tents, packs and counters remain tiny details, not a new caravan village.

sites.name: The Golden Ladle
sites.visual: A dependable working-neighborhood eatery with a modest street entrance, kitchen volume and a practical service edge. Its place among craftspeople should be clear from the adjacent streets.
sites.note: An ordinary urban premises, not a standalone grand banquet hall. Tables and food belong inside or in a tiny yard.

sites.name: West Glowhaven Woods
sites.visual: Shaded woodland outside the western wall, with a maintained outer track, deeper clearing and denser animal cover. Keep a visible difference between the accessible fringe and interior thickets.
sites.note: No obligatory monster icons or new fort. This is woodland, not a second settlement.

sites.name: Gryffin Tail Academy
sites.visual: A cyan-bannered academy with an entrance square, orderly lecture wings, research rooms and a sheltered reading garden. A small training court adds a different outdoor shape to the academic buildings.
sites.note: Seminar rooms, dining, dormitories and game rooms are parts of one campus. Academic calm need not mean bare or featureless architecture.

sites.name: West Greyfield
sites.visual: The western half of the poor settlement outside the southern walls: patched roofs, close-built modest homes and rough lanes. Its texture is less orderly and less affluent than the city inside.
sites.note: It continues toward East Greyfield. Keep it inhabited and extensive enough to be a neighborhood, rather than a single ruin or isolated shack.

sites.name: Hermit's hut
sites.visual: A very small dwelling on a wooded ridge beyond the southwestern city approaches, reached by an uneven footpath. Sparse construction and surrounding woodland make it feel removed from city life.
sites.note: The pin sits exactly on a region boundary. Draw one hut, with the path and vegetation continuing naturally across the tile edge.

sites.name: City Guard Headquarters
sites.visual: A practical city-guard headquarters with a public reporting frontage and an adjoining briefing or drill yard. Keep controlled service access distinct from ordinary public streets.
sites.note: One civic compound in the working city, not a massive prison fortress. Wraith Island remains separate.

sites.name: The Farmer's Exchange
sites.visual: A produce-trading place with scales, cart access, a covered trading edge and practical loading room. It connects rural goods to the central city markets.
sites.note: Use a compact working yard or market-hall footprint. Nearby ordinary shops should not all become farm buildings.

sites.name: The Eternal Crucible
sites.visual: A great public arena with a central competition floor, steep tiered stands and a ring-shaped concourse. Entrances and supporting practice or medical spaces sit around its perimeter.
sites.note: One arena complex. Pillar, planted, ice, stair and shallow-water bout layouts are alternative arrangements of its fighting spaces, not five additional colosseums.

sites.name: Four Sages Bazaar
sites.visual: A civic market square centers on one fountain and the founders' monument, framed by north, east, south and west arcades. The monument commemorates four founding archmages.
sites.note: Use a small four-figure sculptural group as a proposed visual reading of the monument. Keep it one shared fountain, not four remote plazas or four giant towers.

sites.name: Merchant's Row
sites.visual: A continuous eastward extension of the bazaar's commercial streets, lined with shopfronts, awnings and busy pedestrian approaches.
sites.note: Render as a street ensemble rather than one monumental market building. Use small roof masses and a clear walkable lane.

sites.name: Violet Thread
sites.visual: A compact tailor's shop with a fitting-room frontage and space for alterations behind it. Cloth-colored awnings or hanging textiles can distinguish it subtly.
sites.note: One ordinary storefront; the shop name does not require an entirely violet building.

sites.name: The Everlight Public Library
sites.visual: A public library with an orderly reading-hall volume, broad windows and a practical street entrance. Smaller offices and shelves sit within the main building.
sites.note: A notable civic hall but much smaller than an academy precinct. No additional university campus is implied.

sites.name: Adventurer's Guild - Glowhaven Branch
sites.visual: A welcoming timber-and-stone guild hall with honey-colored beams, warm geometric stained glass and a controlled rear practice yard. A broad public entrance serves adventurers and clients.
sites.note: The reception, request boards, common tables, appraisal bench and offices are inside one hall. It is neither an inn nor a second arena.

sites.name: The Perfumed Rose
sites.visual: A small perfumery and household-alchemy shop with a sheltered sample counter or glazed frontage and a preparation space behind.
sites.note: Refined but compact. Do not grow an enormous rose garden or distillery around the name alone.

sites.name: Roseberry Inn
sites.visual: A lived-in city inn with a substantial common-room volume, upper lodging rooms and a modest service yard. Warm windows and an ordinary street-facing entrance suit its function.
sites.note: A small-to-medium urban building, not a resort estate. Bunks and private rooms are inside the same premises.

sites.name: The Carpenter's Measure
sites.visual: A city carpentry shop with a long practical workroom, stacked-timber service edge and ordinary street-facing entrance.
sites.note: Keep lumber piles and workbenches as secondary yard details. It is not a rural logging camp.

sites.name: The Grand Approach
sites.visual: A broad straight avenue runs from the Main City Gate toward Four Sages Bazaar. Its clear sightline and connected frontage make it one of the city's main organizing routes.
sites.note: Treat the pin as a point along a linear avenue. Its full extent joins the two named endpoints rather than ending at the marker.

sites.name: The Silver Anvil
sites.visual: A metalworking and finishing shop with a more formal consultation frontage and a workroom behind. Practical commissioning distinguishes it from a simple weapon stall.
sites.note: A separate workshop from Blackstone Smithy, of comparable ordinary scale. Avoid an enormous freestanding anvil icon.

sites.name: Blackstone Smithy
sites.visual: A functional smithy with a forge chimney, working yard and practical counter or street entrance. Separate the hot workshop volume from the public edge.
sites.note: Small craft premises within the urban grain. Forge glow is a subtle accent, not a volcano or factory district the size of the city.

sites.name: Hide & Hammer
sites.visual: A leatherworks shop combining a public display frontage with cutting and finishing space behind it. A small drying or service courtyard is a reasonable exterior interpretation.
sites.note: One working-city building. Do not infer a slaughterhouse or a large tannery landscape from the name.

sites.name: East Greyfield
sites.visual: The eastern continuation of Greyfield outside the southern wall. Narrow lanes and close-set, worn homes show limited means without turning the district into deserted rubble.
sites.note: Join it visually to West Greyfield while retaining local street variation. Neither half is a separate distant village.

sites.name: Crooked Tankard
sites.visual: A city taproom with a convivial common-room frontage, hearth chimney and practical entrance from the street.
sites.note: One tavern among the surrounding houses. Do not turn its whole block into an enormous tankard-shaped building.

sites.name: East City Gate
sites.visual: A guarded eastern arch links the walled city with the working shore and harbor-side approaches. Connect its road to the coastal network.
sites.note: One gate in the same wall circuit as the West and Main gates, not a separate border fortress.

sites.name: Eastbloom Residences
sites.visual: Middle-class homes near Dragon Hoard Academy, slightly more polished and orderly than average city housing. Maintained small gardens and controlled lanes express its character.
sites.note: Use a neighborhood of human-scale houses, not one vast luxury palace or an additional town wall.

sites.name: The Compassmaker
sites.visual: A small city instrument workshop with a precise, practical storefront and repair benches behind it. Fine metalwork and window light can suggest its craft.
sites.note: One modest shop. The compasses are interior objects and should not become a huge compass rose on the ground.

sites.name: Willowbend Residential District
sites.visual: A middle- and working-class neighborhood of ordinary homes, shared lanes and everyday services. Roof spacing and small courtyards distinguish blocks without making every home unique at master scale.
sites.note: A broad lived-in housing patch, not a single named house. Use a quieter material vocabulary than the court estates.

sites.name: Dragon Hoard Academy
sites.visual: A yellow-and-gold academy precinct with a high entrance gallery, exhibition and laboratory wings, training court and a modest roof-level observatory.
sites.note: Keep academic displays within the galleries and one coherent campus. The name does not imply a dragon skeleton, dragon lair or treasure mountain.

sites.name: The Jade Cup Teahouse
sites.visual: A calm city teahouse with an inviting small entrance and a quieter interior arrangement. A tiny courtyard is a permissible visual interpretation if room allows.
sites.note: Keep it in the city streets. Its name alone does not prescribe foreign monumental architecture or a vast tea estate.

sites.name: Pebblewick
sites.visual: A small coastal town outside the eastern walls, with modest homes, local lanes and access to the water. It provides the inhabited setting for Seabreeze Inn just across the region edge.
sites.note: Distinct from southwestern Pebbletown and southeastern Brookmeadow. Keep the shore settlement visible but much smaller than Glowhaven City.

sites.name: Main City Gate
sites.visual: The largest city gate anchors the southern threshold and the start of the great avenue. Give it a broad passable arch, flanking defensive masonry and a clear road out to Greyfield and the farms.
sites.note: Its silhouette is larger than the other gates, but attached to the same city wall. This pin is the main gate's ground entrance.

sites.name: Seabreeze Inn
sites.visual: A small coastal inn in Pebblewick, with lodging above or behind a public eating room and a straightforward approach from the shore lanes.
sites.note: Its pin is in the neighboring coast region but belongs to the same settlement as Pebblewick. Do not create a second town to contain the inn.

sites.name: Crescent Shores
sites.visual: A curved stretch of eastern beaches with dunes, sheltered coves and a visible dry shore route. Leave uninterrupted sand and water between the few settlements.
sites.note: A coastline feature, not another village. The Crescent Shores pin is only an anchor within a longer beach.

sites.name: Gullwatch Reefs
sites.visual: Low exposed reefs, tidal pools and seabird nesting rocks sit off the eastern shore. Narrow usable channels separate the rock groups.
sites.note: No large buildings or castles. Use water clarity, pale rock and a few tiny birds rather than a giant gull emblem.

sites.name: Splinterwake Wreck
sites.visual: A broken merchant hull lies caught among sharp eastern rocks. Low water reveals portions of its deck and cargo spaces, with deep water nearby.
sites.note: A grounded wreck at ship scale, not an intact enormous warship. The mobile kraken has no permanently occupied building or fixed nest here.

sites.name: Moonarch Isle
sites.visual: A small rocky island holds a weathered stone arch, low foundations, salt-resistant plants and fragments of paving above a pebble landing.
sites.note: The arch is an inert ruin. Keep it smaller than inhabited islands and do not depict an active portal beam or a whole ruined metropolis.

sites.name: Stillback Isle
sites.visual: A sheltered low-rock island has a small beach, nesting shelf and the resting place of Mauruun, the enormous passive turtle. Weathered shell plates can resemble a low living rise.
sites.note: Its habitat remains the durable site. If the turtle is visible, make the head and shell a restrained secondary discovery, never a whole new continent.

sites.name: Pinewater Woods
sites.visual: Pine-shaded paths and a moss clearing follow the river's wooded western side. A usable open river edge contrasts with tighter trees farther inland.
sites.note: Keep river access continuous. Webs or animal signs are tiny optional details, not a web-covered giant dungeon.

sites.name: Pebbletown
sites.visual: A small southwestern town outside Glowhaven's walls, with a town green, market corner and modest homes along connecting lanes.
sites.note: Keep it distinct from Pebblewick and Brookmeadow. It is a smaller settlement, with ordinary homes at the same physical scale as city homes.

sites.name: Pinewater River
sites.visual: A winding river runs through wooded valley banks, linking crossings, farms and Pebbletown's approaches. A ford, a river bend and a bank trail provide distinct usable stretches.
sites.note: Its pin marks a corridor, not the river's entire shape or source. The Disused Pump House is one small riverside structure within this location, not an additional major landmark.

sites.name: Caravan Outpost
sites.visual: A practical staging yard contains wagons, a few trade stalls and a roadside shelter beside the southern Pinewater route.
sites.note: A modest working stop, not a new walled trading city. Wagons and sheds remain comparable in size to other ordinary buildings.

sites.name: Thistlebank Alchemy Cottage
sites.visual: A low working cottage with a small herb plot, a warm copper workroom and a domestic front entrance. Modest planting beds support a household and practical alchemy.
sites.note: One tiny rural premises at a region boundary. Do not enlarge it to a manor, greenhouse palace or industrial plant.

sites.name: Shadowspire
sites.visual: A narrow secluded wizard's tower stands in a woodland pocket off the cultivated country's edge. A small outer clearing, brass-bound door and twisting trail establish its quiet approach.
sites.note: It is a minor skyline accent compared with the Evertree and city institutions. The private portal and impossible household realm are inside or beyond it, not separate Glowhaven landmasses.

sites.name: Glowhaven Farmlands
sites.visual: Cultivated grain and vegetable strips, small homesteads and irrigation branches spread beyond Greyfield and the southern city roads. Farm tracks connect the plots to the wider countryside.
sites.note: Fields, not buildings, occupy most of its footprint. Keep scattered roofs small and avoid filling the open farmland with ceremonial ruins.

sites.name: Seaward Overlook
sites.visual: A grassy coastal cliff has a sheltered sitting place among wind-shaped trees and an exposed sea-facing ledge.
sites.note: A terrain viewpoint, not an observation tower, monument or luxury lodge.

sites.name: Starlark Abbey
sites.visual: White stone and a small bell tower rise above the southern river country. A chapel, hospice and guest wing cluster around a pilgrim court, with a working kitchen garden.
sites.note: A modest abbey devoted to Avelune, Lady of Returning Light. Keep it well below the city campuses in footprint; the hospitable grounds are not a second city.

sites.name: Greenrush Estuary
sites.visual: Shallow tidal channels, reed beds and pale sandbars spread where the river meets the eastern sea. A small skiff landing, raised reedwalk, boat supports and field shelter serve practical work.
sites.note: This is a broad wetland with very few structures. Show actual open channels; do not replace the estuary with a large port city.

sites.name: Old Southwatch
sites.visual: An old stone lookout rises from a forested southern slope, with a root-crossed approach, a habitable lower room and a damaged upper walk.
sites.note: A single modest tower or lookout remnant. It does not command an active garrison or justify another fortress town.

sites.name: Longgrass Crossroads
sites.visual: Three dirt roads meet in open downs near the river bridge and Brookmeadow approach. A worn roofed shelter, bench and cart pull-off mark the junction.
sites.note: No paved highway or triumphal square. The pin sits almost on a northern region edge; draw continuous roads across that seam.

sites.name: Wrenhill Windmill
sites.visual: A working windmill turns above scattered grain plots on Brookmeadow's western approach. A small mill yard and wagon waiting space sit around its base.
sites.note: Keep the mill a compact useful landmark, not an enormous wind-farm monument. Nearby houses retain the same ordinary building scale.

sites.name: Brookmeadow
sites.visual: A small southeastern farming village gathers modest houses around a green, with crop plots, working yards, mill lanes and a riverward approach. Mihana's cottage is one ordinary home off Mill Lane.
sites.note: This is the established rural starting village, not a new port. Its mill-lane name does not create a second giant windmill; Wrenhill Windmill is separately pinned to the west.
